intro.ascent: Dawn at the launch pad. The crew arrives at the tower: load the fuel, climb aboard, close the hatch and talk to mission control before the countdown.
intro.landing: The "seven minutes of terror": the ship enters the Martian atmosphere on its own and you give every order on time.
intro.marsAscent: The ascent vehicle waits in Gale crater. Load the propellant, climb aboard, pressurize the cabin and lift off: the neater you fly, the more fuel is left for the trip home.
intro.reentry: Earth is close. We must enter shield first and open the parachutes on time.
checklist.title: Checklist: Go or No-Go?
checklist.hint: Check every system before leaving. Anything not green can be fixed with spare parts or flown at risk.
checklist.detail.green: Working fine. Confirm it with GO.
checklist.detail.repair: Repair: use {cost} spare parts and it turns green.
checklist.detail.repairOne: Repair: use 1 spare part and it turns green.
checklist.detail.noSpares: Not enough spare parts to repair it (you need {cost}, you have {have}).
checklist.detail.risk.yellow: Risk it: keep your spare parts, but that stage will be harder (smaller green zone).
checklist.detail.risk.red: Risk it: keep your spare parts, but that stage will be much harder (tiny green zone).
checklist.detail.done.repair: Repaired with spare parts: it's green now.
checklist.detail.done.risk: Flying at risk: its stage will be harder. Focus there!
checklist.detail.pending: Confirm every system to start the maneuver.
checklist.detail.ready: Every system is green. Good luck, crew!
checklist.detail.readyRiskOne: You're leaving with 1 system at risk: its stage will be harder.
checklist.detail.readyRisk: You're leaving with {n} systems at risk: those stages will be harder.
stage.hint: Press SPACE (or click) when the marker is in the green zone
stage.miss: Outside the zone: fuel was used to correct it. Keep going!
stage.ascent.boosterSeparation.fact: The side boosters used up their fuel and drop away.
stage.ascent.stageSeparation.fact: The first stage drops away and the ship gets lighter.
stage.landing.entry.fact: The ship enters at about 20,000 km/h and the heat shield reaches about 1,300 °C, like Perseverance's did in 2021.
stage.landing.parachute.fact: The parachute opens 11 km above the ground at about 1,500 km/h: faster than sound on Mars!
stage.landing.heatShieldSeparation.fact: The shield is not needed anymore: it drops so the radar can see the ground.
stage.landing.descentEngines.fact: The engines slow the ship down so it touches the ground gently.
stage.marsAscent.orbitInsertion.fact: The ship settles into orbit to begin the trip home.
stage.reentry.orientShield.fact: The heat shield must go first, like an umbrella against the heat.
stage.reentry.reentry.fact: Artemis I's Orion capsule came back at about 40,000 km/h: its shield reached about 2,800 °C and the radio cut out for a little while.
stage.reentry.splashdown.fact: The parachutes slow the capsule to less than 32 km/h so it lands softly in the sea.
result.title: Maneuver complete
result.landing: You landed {km} km from the base.
result.landingFar: Farther away means more trips outside, with more dust and more radiation.
result.signal: The landing signal takes between 3 and 22 minutes to reach Earth, depending on where the planets are. By the time they find out, you will have landed!
result.returnFuel: This fuel is for correcting the course on the way home.
result.vanAllen: Now the ship crosses the Van Allen belts. Look at what Artemis I measured.
result.arrival.stretcher: {name} is carried out on a stretcher: their body got used to low gravity
dust.Moderate: Curiosity sees some dust in the air over Gale today: the bar moves a little faster.
dust.Low: Curiosity sees a lot of dust in the air over Gale today: the bar moves faster.
stage.ascent.fuel.fact: The tanks are filled with very cold fuel. Not too little (it won't reach orbit) and not too much (extra weight).
stage.ascent.board.fact: Each astronaut plugs their suit into the ship's air and fastens the seat belts.
stage.ascent.countdown.fact: A real countdown lasts hours; here you see the last minute: the arm swings away, the beacons light up and water pours under the pad.
stage.ascent.gravityTurn.fact: The rocket slowly tilts to gain sideways speed and stay in orbit.
stage.marsAscent.fuel.fact: Part of the propellant oxygen can be made on Mars from its CO2 air, as MOXIE showed.
stage.marsAscent.board.fact: The crew climbs the service platform with the rock samples safely packed.
stage.marsAscent.countdown.fact: Mars has less gravity than Earth: it takes less push to lift off. Nobody cheers: mission control is light-minutes away.
game.fuel.short: Not enough fuel: extra will be burned
game.fuel.over: Too much: the ship is heavier
game.fuel.overflow: It overflowed! Loading stopped and fuel was lost
game.countdown.late: The engines lit by themselves, a bit late
game.steer.shaky: Lots of shaking: fuel was used to correct
stage.ascent.pressure.fact: With the hatch closed, the cabin fills with air and the crew checks for leaks.
stage.ascent.radioCheck.fact: Mission control tests the radio with the crew before liftoff.
stage.marsAscent.pressure.fact: There is almost no air outside: the cabin must be sealed tight before liftoff.
game.pressure.leaky: There were leaks: air and fuel spent fixing them
game.radio.wrong: Static: mission control repeats the message
game.radio.perfect: Loud and clear: Go for launch!
game.radio.static: Lots of static, but we carry on
game.countdown.wait: Wait: launch comes in the last ten
milestone.armRetract: T-45: the access arm swings away
milestone.beacons: T-30: beacons on, the crowd stands up!
milestone.water: T-15: water pours under the pad to soften the noise
milestone.mastRetract: T-20: the service platform swings away
milestone.dust: T-12: the wind lifts red dust
cinematic.ascent: Dawn on the coast: the crew arrives at the launch pad.
cinematic.marsAscent: Morning in Gale crater: the crew leaves the base for the ascent vehicle.
cinematic.liftoff: Liftoff! There go Vega, Miga, Brote and Senda…
